prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Sentinel Vale ground excludes spacecraft/launch/external processing; delivers predictable-latency, quality-documented imagery. Mission Control Center (Bluebell: local-voice-only) owns authorization/readiness/schedules/routing; contacts require readiness/live-monitoring/post-pass-closure. Flight Dynamics Facility (Mistral: legacy-shift-logs) supplies orbit/maneuver/navigation/visibility/pointing. Mission Planning System converts approved demands/constraints/contact-bookings into plans; Command Validation Gateway must validate uplinks; planning/release segregated. Telemetry Ingest Service receives spacecraft telemetry/contact-status/data-flow indicators; supplies operations/engineering/processing, distinguishing interruptions. Orbit Determination Engine consumes tracking; produces controlled orbit knowledge/Doppler Residual Report. Payload Processing Facility coordinates processing/calibration/quality/distribution. Primary Processing Cluster nominal; Backup Processing Cluster controlled-failover, lower normal routing preference, routinely tested firewall/return paths. Primary-to-Long Term Archive transfers rate-limited during contacts, protecting telemetry/control-plane monitoring. Product Quality Service checks dissemination; archive preserves data/products/evidence; User Services Portal handles search/orders/status/support. Network Control System (Lantern) owns circuit-status, routing/allocations/readiness/contact-records. Ground Network Manager (Juniper: standing-rosters) arbitrates readiness/conflicts/maintenance/staffing; issues Antenna Deicing Notice; pins critical paths before acquisition. Latency-exceedance investigation: carrier, routing, loss, queues, security-inspection before mission-impact declaration. Spacecraft Operations Team owns safety/contact-decisions; Flight Dynamics Team navigation/orbit-maintenance/timing-quality, separates clock bias/tracking error; Payload Calibration Team performance/quality. Cybersecurity Desk monitors/escalates; sends Security Exception Ticket for temporary baseline-deviation. Sites review sensors/endpoint-telemetry/privileged-access/configuration each shift; correlate route/authentication/remote-access/encrypted-volume anomalies. Contingency blocking requires manager/desk coordination protecting contacts/recovery. North S-Band Antenna/South S-Band Antenna interchangeable command/telemetry; Kiruna X-Band Antenna/Svalbard X-Band Antenna dual-path payload-downlink. Redundant terrestrial circuits; restricted/unadvertised administration; authenticated neighbors/approved prefixes/deterministic preferences/controlled adjacencies/preconfigured backups. Class latency budgets include encryption/firewalls; tighter orbit jitter. Daily freeze; changes approved/recorded; safety>timeliness>efficiency; weather/margins constrain contacts. Redundant

New part:
S078: The North S-Band Antenna and South S-Band Antenna are normally assigned for command and low-rate telemetry contacts, while the Kiruna X-Band Antenna and Svalbard X-Band Antenna support high-rate telemetry reception when the visibility geometry and data volume justify their use.
S079: The Network Control System provides the Mission Control Center with antenna status, link configuration, timing references, and routing readiness before each pass begins.
S080: The Telemetry Ingest Service accepts real-time frames, validates basic framing and time continuity, and records reception metadata needed for later operational review.
S081: The Telemetry Ingest Service produces the Pass Replay Packet after a contact when the received stream must be reconstructed for engineering review.
S082: During live operations, the Spacecraft Operations Team monitors spacecraft mode, power state, thermal margins, attitude indicators, command counters, onboard storage, and fault protection messages from the Mission Control Center consoles.
S083: Console displays emphasize deviations from expected state rather than raw parameter volume, because operators must identify safety trends while a contact is still available.
S084: The console lead is responsible for declaring pass status, authorizing planned command execution through the Command Validation Gateway, and pausing the activity when telemetry does not match the expected configuration.
S085: The telemetry engineer verifies reception quality, frame loss, latency, and stream continuity, and advises the console lead when degraded link conditions could affect command confidence.
S086: The spacecraft systems engineer interprets health telemetry, confirms that subsystem states remain within flight rules, and records any anomaly context needed by subsystem specialists.
S087: The Ground Network Manager remains accountable for antenna assignment, ground link availability, and coordination with site operations when weather, equipment status, or routing issues affect a contact.
S088: The Flight Dynamics Team uses tracking measurements and validated time tags from the contact to support orbit assessment at the Flight Dynamics Facility.
S089: The Orbit Determination Engine supports routine state updates and provides the basis for predicting future visibility periods, maneuver planning constraints, and antenna pointing expectations.
S090: Pass reconstruction begins when the contact closes and combines command history, received telemetry timing, ground station status, and operator log entries into a single operational narrative.
S091: The reconstructed pass record is used to confirm whether planned objectives were completed, whether any onboard event occurred outside the timeline, and whether additional engineering analysis is required.
S092: The Payload Processing Facility is also known operationally as Forgehouse in console discussions and shift logs.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
